original_question: Take a composite formed by mixing an isotropic elastic phase with either a void phase or a rigid phase. Can one completely characterize the resulting G-closure, that is, the full set of effective elasticity tensors obtainable from all such microstructures?
target_in_paper: Section 4, Problem 4.1: "Can one complete the characterization of the G-closure for a void (or rigid) phase mixed with an isotropic elastic phase?"
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right open problem almost verbatim: it identifies the correct two-phase setting (an isotropic elastic phase mixed with either void or a rigid phase), and it asks for the complete G-closure, i.e. the full set of attainable effective elasticity tensors rather than only scalar effective moduli. It also stays at the tensorial level, which matches Problem 4.1 rather than the narrower follow-up questions about isotropic (kappa*, mu*) pairs.
missing_details: The paper formulates this as Problem 4.1 in Section 4; it is not one of the Section 1 conjectures/propositions/theorems.
The isotropic elastic constituent is understood to have fixed positive elastic moduli; the problem is not simultaneously varying the constituent material parameters.
The surrounding context makes clear that the G-closure is considered for prescribed phase volume fractions/proportions.
The target is the full set of homogenized effective elasticity tensors, not merely the achievable region of isotropic effective bulk and shear moduli.
The ambient dimension is not restricted to one case in Problem 4.1; the nearby discussion frames the difficulty in both two and three dimensions.
The phrase "void or rigid" means two separate two-phase settings (elastic+void, or elastic+rigid), not a three-phase mixture containing both void and rigid phases.

The draft does not explicitly signal that the paper places this question after noting that substantial progress is known in the void case and in the rigid-phase analogue, but that parts of the G-closure remain unmapped.
refined_question: For prescribed phase volume fractions in spatial dimension d = 2 or 3, fix one constituent to be an isotropic elastic material with fixed positive elastic moduli, and let the second constituent be either void or rigid. What is the complete G-closure, namely the full set of homogenized effective elasticity tensors attainable by arbitrary microgeometries of this two-phase composite?
justification: The draft matches Section 4, Problem 4.1 essentially exactly. The introduction defines the G-closure as the range of effective tensors obtained as the microgeometry varies. In Section 4, Milton first explains that the relevant set is the set of possible elasticity tensors built from two isotropic phases in prescribed volume fractions, notes prior progress for the elastic+void case and for the rigid-phase analogue, and then states Problem 4.1 in almost the same words as your draft. This makes Problem 4.1 the nearest official formulation. It is also clearly the correct target rather than Problems 4.2-4.7, which narrow the discussion to isotropic effective bulk/shear moduli, auxetic limits, or polycrystal subproblems.
